description: Alaska Shoreline Change Tool is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Alaska Department of Natural Resources, Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys; USFWS Coastal Impact Assistance Program; Alaska Ocean Observing System. This interactive map displays historic and predicted shoreline positions throughout Alaska. Users can explore the coasts of the state to see where the shoreline has been in the past, and where it will likely be in the future. Historic shoreline positions were determined from aerial photographs and satellite imagery dating back to the 1950s. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Erosion and Shoreline Recession, Flooding – Coastal. Assets: Natural Areas and Wildlife, Water Infrastructure – General. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
